structure.heading: Segment Momentum, Margin Mix Shift, and FY2026 Investor Guidance
text_content: **Segment Momentum, Margin Mix Shift, and FY2026 Investor Guidance**

Cloud & Subscriptions delivered FY2025 revenue of $5.1B with a segment operating margin of 27.4%, reflecting robust recurring revenue growth and high incremental profitability. Hardware & Devices produced FY2025 revenue of $3.2B and a 10.2% segment operating margin, demonstrating stabilization after targeted cost initiatives and product lifecycle management and improved customer retention.

The mix shift toward higher-margin Cloud & Subscriptions materially improved consolidated profitability in FY2025, increasing weighted average margins while moderating revenue volatility. Segment margin differential—27.4% versus 10.2%—highlights where future investments will prioritize scalable software, data services, and subscription monetization to drive sustained margin expansion across the portfolio over the next several years.

Operational priorities for FY2026 will target cross-segment synergies, supply chain efficiency, and R&D allocation to maximize returns. Specific levers include:
- consolidating cloud infrastructure spend,
- optimizing device production yield, and
- accelerating AI-enabled subscription features.
These actions are intended to capture margin upside and support disciplined capital allocation consistent with oversight.

Looking ahead, FY2026 guidance calls for revenue of $13.3B–$13.8B and operating margin of 19.0%–19.8%, reflecting management's confidence in margin recovery and top-line stability. The company will provide quarterly updates, reconcile segment contributions versus consolidated targets, and maintain transparency on any assumptions regarding macro conditions, pricing, and customer retention metrics for investors globally.

structure.heading: FY2025 Consolidated Financial Performance and Shareholder Returns
text_content: **FY2025 Consolidated Financial Performance and Shareholder Returns**

Full-year FY2025 revenue was $12.4B, up 9% year-over-year, reflecting strength acrsos customer channels, product portfolios, and geographic markets. Revenue performance benefitted from double-digit growth in enterprise software and services, resilient recurring revenue sterams, and recoveries in APAC and EMEA. Management attributes top-line expansion to targeted commercial investments, new contract wins, and price realization initiatives executed druing F2Y025, while retaiinng discilpined customer acquisition costs and improved channel productivity across key segments.

Operational execution delivered margin expansion in FY2025: our operating margin expanded to 18.6% from 16.9% in FY2024, driven by gross margin recovery, productivity programs, and fixed-cost leverage on higher volumes. The finance organization realized structural savings throguh process automation, optimized supply chain contracts, and tighter SG&A discipline. Capital expenditure and R&D investments were rebalanced to prioritize hig-hreturn initiatives while protecting long-term innovation, enabling sustainable margin improvement into FY2026 planning cycles.

Diluted earnings per share for FY2025 were $5.12 versus $4.41 in FY2024, reflecting higher operating income and favorable tax and share-count dynamics. The Board approved a balanced capital allocation approach that included continued quarterly dividends, a $600 million share repurchase authorization, and disciplined reinvestment in growth initiatives. Investor Relations will provide detailed reconciliation and non-GAAP bridges publicly to help analysts model forward EPS sensitivity under multiple revenue and margin scenarios.

sections.heading: Executive Summary
sections.body: Fiscal Year 2025 marked a year of disciplined, margin-led growth for the Company, with total revenue rising 11.8% year over year to $4.27 billion. Expansion in higher-margin subscription and professional services drove operating leverage across the enterprise. Operating income increased 19.6% to $812 million, reflecting continued cost optimization and improved revenue mix. Management believes these results position the Company to sustain profitable expansion into FY2026.

sections.heading: Revenue Composition and Growth Drivers
sections.body: Subscription and recurring services revenue grew 18.4% to $2.31 billion, now representing 54% of total revenue compared to 50% in FY2024. Growth was fueled by strong net retention of 112% and the addition of 640 new enterprise clients across North America and EMEA. Professional services revenue increased 9.1%, supported by large-scale digital transformation engagements. Product hardware revenue declined modestly by 2.7%, consistent with the Company’s strategy to prioritize higher-margin recurring streams.

sections.heading: Operating Margin and Cost Discipline
sections.body: Operating margin expanded 130 basis points to 19.0%, reflecting improved gross margin and disciplined expense management. Gross margin improved to 61.5%, driven primarily by scale efficiencies in cloud infrastructure and automation within customer support operations. Selling, general and administrative expenses grew at a slower pace than revenue, increasing 6.3% year over year. These efficiencies demonstrate the scalability of the Company’s platform-centric operating model.

sections.heading: Earnings and Capital Allocation
sections.body: Diluted earnings per share rose 22.4% to $3.87, benefiting from higher operating income and a 2% reduction in weighted-average shares outstanding through share repurchases. Free cash flow reached $745 million, up 17% from the prior year, enabling continued investment in product innovation while returning $210 million to shareholders via dividends and buybacks. The Company ended FY2025 with $1.4 billion in cash and short-term investments and net debt to EBITDA of 1.1x.

sections.heading: Segment Performance and FY2026 Outlook
sections.body: The Digital Platforms segment delivered revenue growth of 16%, while the Enterprise Solutions segment grew 8%, supported by multi-year contract renewals and cross-sell initiatives. Management expects FY2026 revenue between $4.65 billion and $4.75 billion, with operating margin projected to expand by an additional 50 to 80 basis points. Continued momentum in subscription adoption and disciplined expense control are anticipated to drive sustained earnings growth. Strategic priorities for FY2026 include accelerated AI-enabled service offerings and expansion into select Asia-Pacific markets.

structure.full_text:
Fiscal Year 2025 Annual Performance Overview
For the Year Ended 31 December 2025 | Investor Relations Update | Issued 18 February 2026

Section Executive Summary
Fiscal Year 2025 marked a year of disciplined, margin-led growth for the Company, with total revenue rising 11.8% year over year to $4.27 billion. Expansion in higher-margin subscription and professional services drove operating leverage across the enterprise. Operating income increased 19.6% to $812 million, reflecting continued cost optimization and improved revenue mix. Management believes these results position the Company to sustain profitable expansion into FY2026.

Section Revenue Composition and Growth Drivers
Subscription and recurring services revenue grew 18.4% to $2.31 billion, now representing 54% of total revenue compared to 50% in FY2024. Growth was fueled by strong net retention of 112% and the addition of 640 new enterprise clients across North America and EMEA. Professional services revenue increased 9.1%, supported by large-scale digital transformation engagements. Product hardware revenue declined modestly by 2.7%, consistent with the Company’s strategy to prioritize higher-margin recurring streams.

Section Operating Margin and Cost Discipline
Operating margin expanded 130 basis points to 19.0%, reflecting improved gross margin and disciplined expense management. Gross margin improved to 61.5%, driven primarily by scale efficiencies in cloud infrastructure and automation within customer support operations. Selling, general and administrative expenses grew at a slower pace than revenue, increasing 6.3% year over year. These efficiencies demonstrate the scalability of the Company’s platform-centric operating model.

Section Earnings and Capital Allocation
Diluted earnings per share rose 22.4% to $3.87, benefiting from higher operating income and a 2% reduction in weighted-average shares outstanding through share repurchases. Free cash flow reached $745 million, up 17% from the prior year, enabling continued investment in product innovation while returning $210 million to shareholders via dividends and buybacks. The Company ended FY2025 with $1.4 billion in cash and short-term investments and net debt to EBITDA of 1.1x.

Section Segment Performance and FY2026 Outlook
The Digital Platforms segment delivered revenue growth of 16%, while the Enterprise Solutions segment grew 8%, supported by multi-year contract renewals and cross-sell initiatives. Management expects FY2026 revenue between $4.65 billion and $4.75 billion, with operating margin projected to expand by an additional 50 to 80 basis points. Continued momentum in subscription adoption and disciplined expense control are anticipated to drive sustained earnings growth. Strategic priorities for FY2026 include accelerated AI-enabled service offerings and expansion into select Asia-Pacific markets.
